title: Takt Victims' Association
paragraphs: “Right?”
Rival speaks up, looking as if she hasn’t quite gotten her point across to her Assistant.
“If you want, Gaelion can help Big Sis get even stronger. Or do you want to study all sorts of things?”
Rival goes on to suggest things like arranging for her to study abroad in Siltvelt or Faubrey. Come to think of it, there are schools like that in this world, aren’t there?
“That’s not it. I’ve realized I need to try harder… using my own strength! As an older sister, I can’t let my younger sister beat me!”
“Is that so?”
Rival looks completely confused, as if she doesn’t quite understand what the Assistant is saying. On the other hand, Father, who was watching this exchange, looks like he’s caught on to something.
“Gaelion-chan. It seems Wyndia-chan wants to do something as an older sister—it’s not about level, knowledge, or experience. I think you should just let her do as she pleases.”
“Hm? Is that so?”
“Yes. You understand perfectly well, don’t you?”
The assistant speaks to Father in a condescending tone, completely out of line with her station. It’s a bit irritating.
“I’m going home to take that step. At least see me off.”
“But… are you okay, big sis?”
“Don’t make me say it again!”
Whoa! The assistant has turned her hostility toward Rival. Heh! She’s the one everyone hates!
“Gaelion-chan. Wyndia-chan and I… we had a fight—”
“Vvvvvuuuuu… Gau!”
Just as Father was about to say something, the assistant radiated a murderous aura and growled and barked at him. After all, the Assistant is a wild child at heart. Of course she’d growl.
“Ah… I get it. Then I’ll take you home. Naofumi, I’ll be gone for a bit.”
“Once you drop her off near her house, you can come right back here. Oh… I’ll talk to Dad for you.”
“Is that okay?”
“Yes, but you have to promise me. Once you’ve finished everything you need to do, you have to come back for sure!”
“Of course!”

It seems the Assistant has given up on Rival. It looks like the plan is to try to persuade him after he’s messed things up on his own and hit a wall. And so, right there at the end of the meeting, Rival decided to take flight from Melromarc toward the eastern mountain range. Now, it’s just before departure. As Father sees her off, the Assistant calls out to him.
“I’m going to be patient this time, but if anything happens to Gaelion, I won’t forgive you! You’d better take good care of him!　If you do anything to make him cry, I won’t forgive you!”
But how exactly is one supposed to make Rival cry any more than he already has? Father has already lost his virginity. Still, she had to be on guard to make sure her virginity wasn’t taken.
“Of course I’ll make him cry! Hahaha!”
As I replied like that, my assistant furrowed her brow in puzzlement and looked at me.
“I’ve thought that guy was weird for a while now, but I’m pretty sure he’s got something all mixed up.”
“Ah… yeah, just ignore him. He’s not a bad person, and thanks to Motoyasu-kun, Gaelion and I were able to meet in the first place.”
“It’s too mean to deny it.”
“Anyway, just like him, I won’t forgive him!”
“Yeah. I know.”
“Well then, let’s get going!”
With a flutter, Rival spread his wings and soared high into the sky. Hehe, things will be quiet for a while now.
“Come on, Sakura-chan! You’re going to get petted by Father ten times more than Rival did!”
“But didn’t Sakura-chan just go over to Melty-chan’s place?”
“What did you say?!”

Sakura-chan, this is exactly the kind of moment when you need to boost your friendship level with Father. Ugh… but perhaps this free-spirited nature is exactly what makes Sakura-chan—who is also Filo-tan—so endearing.

It seems the issue regarding the Spirit Tortoise has been resolved in that sort of way. Indeed, just as Rival said, the Spirit Tortoise’s revival—which would normally have occurred if we hadn’t intervened—didn’t happen.

And so, our days passed as we continued dealing with the Shieldfreeden issue and searching for Ren. Of course, I also went off on my own to track down whoever had done that to the Filolial producer’s ranch. However, I found no clues whatsoever.
Some time has passed since then. Various cases have come our way. Among them, we ended up taking on one of the bigger ones.
“So that’s the island where the remnants of Takt are likely hiding…”
“It seems so.”
We were looking out from the ship’s deck at the target island. It was one of the islands east of Shieldfreeden.
That was yesterday. Rival summoned us and Father to inform us that a location where Takt’s remnants were highly likely to be hiding had been pinpointed.
“How did you manage to track them down?”
“This information also came from the Takt Victims’ Association. The person who provided this information is a victim whose very story brings tears to your eyes.”

After saying that, Rival introduced the informant to Father. He was a man who looked quite worn out. But I could sense something sharp in his gaze—something reminiscent of Father from the First World. That look… it’s definitely the gaze of someone trustworthy.
“To the Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes… thank you for listening to my story today, Tommy Mistira.”
“U-uh-huh.”
Father nods, seeming slightly intimidated by the man whose gaze resembles that of Father from the first world.
“Based on this information, I ask that you eradicate the remaining Takt forces. That is my sole wish, and it is what the other victims are seeking as well.”
“Um…”
Father turns his gaze toward Rival, as if asking a question.
“It goes without saying that we must eliminate the remaining members of Takt.”
When I nodded in agreement with the man’s statement, he nodded vigorously as if to show his trust in me and bowed his head to me.
“It’s practically thanks to you, Spear Hero, that I’m even here… Please, use your power to bring God’s wrath down upon these evil ones.”
Oh! He’s a guy who really gets it. Those Takt remnants are vermin that need to be exterminated. There’s no doubt about that!
“Um… I think we’d better hear the whole story.”
For some reason, Father said this with a troubled look on his face. Well, given the look on his face, there must be some deeper circumstances at play.
“It might take a little while to explain all that. First of all… it is my—no, it is the wish of those who share my cause—that you prioritize bringing down God’s hammer as soon as possible.”
“I-it feels like a lot of people are involved? Besides the government’s search.”
“Yes. The victims whose lives were twisted by Takt have joined forces and are taking action in various countries.”
“Huh… Sounds like it’s turned into quite an impressive organization. So, about that—you said you tracked down the hideout of the remaining Takt members…”
“Yes.”
The informant unfolds a world map and points to a certain location. It looks like an island in the ocean.

"There’s no doubt that remnants of Takt’s forces are hiding out on this island. I hear that before he died, Takt bought the entire island and renamed it Seven Island, but locally it’s known as Demon King Island or Seven-Split Island."
“W-wow, that’s a pretty sinister story.”

“Yes… Apparently, according to ancient legends, this is where the Seven Star Heroes defeated the Demon King. But the Demon King was immortal and had the ability to resurrect, so the heroes were forced to tear him into seven pieces and bury them throughout the island to seal him away.”
That’s a terrifyingly sinister tale. It really does feel like the kind of island where such legends linger.
“An immortal monster, is it? Even if it’s a creature like that, I’ve got a way to take it on!”
“It’s pretty impressive, in a way, that you, Motoyasu-kun, can boast that you can defeat something like that.”

“Well, I think it’s just some guy pretending to be a tough, immortal Demon King. It’s only natural that a hero would target something like that for extermination. It’s because it defies the laws of nature.”
“…Come to think of it, as long as Motoyasu-kun is around, Gaelion-chan feels kind of like she’s immortal, too.”
“That’s what makes her a dragon—and Gaelion.”
“To begin with, even so-called ‘undead’ aren’t immortal down to their very souls, so we just need to rip it out and kill it. Rival, if I could just kill you, I wouldn’t be in this much trouble.”
“Hehehe, that’s right.”
It’s a monstrous dragon parasitizing my spear! How can I purify it!?
“That said, in Gaelion’s case, it’s a pseudo-immortality—her body and soul can actually be destroyed, so it’s a bit different. It’s just part of the Dragon Emperor’s nature.”
“I’d think that’d be enough, though…”
“Well, I won’t deny that I could kill her even if she were truly immortal.”
I possess the Spear 0, which can even kill gods. Father from the First World told me so. Apparently, it’s effective against those who are immortal or ageless.
“It’s true—there’s no doubt that the Spear Hero could defeat even someone who’s immortal and ageless.”
For some reason, Rival agrees with me. Isn’t he just grudgingly admitting it?
“I do think declaring you can defeat them is impressive in many ways, though…”
“Lord Kitamura, who can state with absolute certainty that he can slay such suspicious monsters… might indeed be a hero.”
Éclair seems convinced. She’s become quite reasonable.
“Well, it’s sort of a blessing from what Naofumi did in the first world. Gaelion can sense that too, so there’s no doubt about it.”
“Huh… Well, let’s just set aside the island’s legends for now.”
“I think that’s for the best… Look, this guy’s face is practically screaming, ‘Kill the Takt remnants as soon as possible!’”
Panda is looking at the male informant with a troubled expression. That’s right. It’s rude to keep someone who harbors a grudge waiting.
“Um… why are you so determined to wipe out the remaining Takt members?”
Father is asking the man to explain the situation. Well, I’m sure it’s within the realm of imagination.
“…It’s a long story. It’s not just me—there are many others like me as well—”

And so the man began to speak. Apparently, this man had a steady job in Shieldfreeden and lived his life earnestly, making sincerity his motto. Blessed with a beautiful wife and a growing, adorable daughter, his life was apparently going smoothly. However, misfortune struck.

Apparently, his wife fell ill, and to cure her, he needed a medicinal herb that was so difficult to obtain that even adventurers struggled to find it. To save his wife, the man desperately scraped together money and placed a request with the Adventurers’ Guild, but there was no word that they’d obtained the herb… He even went so far as to personally beg renowned adventurers for help. However, the location was a problem… Apparently, the herb grows in the nests of griffins and dragons or something like that.

Well, it’d be tough for an ordinary adventurer. We can take them down easily enough, but for the folks in this world, they’re pretty tough opponents. Back when my gear wasn’t fully upgraded, I wouldn’t have wanted to venture into such a dangerous area either.

Come to think of it, back in my gaming days, even some of my hunting grounds were way too dangerous… but for me now, even the weakest enemies are a piece of cake. When you look at it that way, the power inflation is pretty wild. Anyway, it seems that medicinal herb growing in such a dangerous place was necessary to treat my wife.

And then—call it a stroke of luck or a series of misfortunes piling up—Takt apparently heard about the situation after being lured in by my daughter’s good looks. If Takt had just gone and picked the medicinal herbs normally and cured my wife’s illness, the story wouldn’t have gotten so complicated, and the misfortune would have simply passed. But, well, this is Takt we’re talking about. It seems he came up with a solution that was nothing short of sickening—and full of twists and turns.

It was all fine up until he actually gathered the medicinal herb, but then, right in front of this man, he apparently said, “I ended up picking some weeds instead!” while blatantly flashing the herb and using it as dragon feed. The man begged Takt to spare the herbs, offering all his possessions and bowing his head, but Takt wouldn’t budge an inch. Just as the man was about to walk away, he found himself cornered. If he missed this chance, his wife might not survive.

At that moment, Takt took a single leaf of the medicinal herb and stomped it underfoot right before the man’s eyes. The man, losing all self-control, reached out toward the herb. Immediately afterward, it seems he lost consciousness.

When he next regained consciousness, he was in the kingdom’s detention center, reportedly imprisoned as punishment for flying into a rage and lunging at Takt. Although it was true that he had lunged at Tact, he claimed he had no such intention; however, the soldiers refused to accept his explanation, and a trial was held. The man was convicted of various crimes, including robbery, his property was confiscated, and he was sentenced to hard labor. Even so, he continued to worry about the safety of his wife and daughter, clinging to the faint hope that at least they were safe.

That’s when Takt came to visit him, bringing his wife and daughter, who had both recovered. The man was relieved, thinking that Takt—having sensed the situation—had saved his wife’s life, but apparently, that’s when the real hell began. Believe it or not, it’s said that his wife and daughter had abandoned him to run off with Takt; they apparently slammed a letter of severance in his face and walked away laughing.

“What did you do for me when I was suffering from illness? Takt, who risked his life to get me medicine, is a million times better than you!　“That’s why, goodbye, you pathetic man… Just the thought of having been with you makes me want to vomit.”
“Goodbye, uncool criminal dad. Cool Takt-san will take care of us, so don’t ever come near us again.”

Apparently, these were the last words from his wife and daughter. It’s said that at that point, the man realized everything. He realized that Takt had approached them with his sights set on his wife and daughter, and had framed him for a crime he didn’t commit. At the same time, the man felt a murderous rage toward his wife—who had ditched him for Takt despite his desperate efforts to provide for her—and the story goes that he was forced into hard labor.
What an absolute pig. Just like me back in the day, didn’t this man have his eyes completely clouded to have married such a woman? But I don’t think it’s a case of “you reap what you sow.”

“And so, Takt’s true nature has been exposed for all to see, and I have thus been proven innocent. But even though Takt is dead, his remnants remain! So I’ve sworn to take revenge on Takt’s remnants, which is why I found this lead and am reporting it. My wish is to make that woman and her daughter suffer the hell on earth!”
